display.purpose: English and Ukrainian vocabulary words in study sessions. The product made visible.

headline.purpose: Page-level titles: deck name in hero, home greeting. One per view.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Ambient resting shadow. Primary button at rest only.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Hover lift for cards (+translateY(-3px)), structural floating for dropdown panels.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Full-screen modals and auth card. Heavy, intentional, floating layers only.

shadows.name: shadow-glow
shadows.purpose: Focus ring for inputs, selection ring for quiz/match elements. State, not decoration.

narrative.overview:
Late evening. One browser tab. Vocabulary lists in front of you. The interface is the ambient light: always present, never competing with the content it holds. This system is built for a single user who knows what they want: to review vocabulary efficiently and leave. Every surface is subordinate to the word on the screen.

The deep indigo charcoal backgrounds create a contained, low-stimulation environment. The single emerald accent communicates presence, progress, and correctness without demanding attention. When you look at this interface, you notice the vocabulary first. The UI second, if at all.

This system rejects educational software language: no streaks, no mascots, no confetti, no gamified reward loops. It also rejects generic product darkness: no gradient hero panels, no neon accents, no identical icon-grid stat banners. Depth comes from tonal surface steps, not decoration. Feedback comes from color and shape, not celebration choreography.
keyCharacteristics: Single emerald accent; used sparingly across all surfaces
Four tonal surface levels replace shadows for structural depth
Inter only, hierarchy through scale and weight contrast alone
Animations: state-driven, short, ease-out; never choreographed

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The emerald accent (#10b981) appears on no more than 15% of any given screen. Its scarcity is its power. Every additional use must answer: 'Is this the most important thing on this screen right now?'

rules.name: The Status-Only Rule
rules.body: Success (#22c55e), danger (#ef4444), and warning (#f59e0b) are reserved strictly for feedback states: correct, incorrect, caution. They are never decorative accents or brand color substitutes.

rules.name: The Weight Bridge Rule
rules.body: Each typographic step must differ by at least 1.25x in size or one full weight grade. A heading at 18px/500 adjacent to body at 15px/400 is too flat to read as hierarchy.

rules.name: The Single Face Rule
rules.body: Inter carries the full typographic system. No secondary or decorative typeface is added. Emphasis through weight and size, never through font-family switching.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface at rest never has a box-shadow unless it is a floating layer (modal, toast) or has the ambient-resting exception (primary button). Hover and focus add shadows; presence does not.

rules.name: The Glow-for-State Rule
rules.body: Colored glow rings (accent, success, danger) are state indicators, not decorative treatments. A glowing element is telling the user something: focused, correct, or wrong.

dos: Do use the emerald accent on no more than 15% of any given screen. Count before adding.
Do let the English word dominate at 36px/600 in accent color during study sessions.
Do use tonal surface steps (base to surface to elevated to subtle) for structural depth before reaching for shadows.
Do keep all transitions at 200ms ease-in-out; use cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) for entrances.
Do surface keyboard shortcuts as kbd elements wherever they exist.
Do use uppercase labels (11px, 0.08em tracking) only for column headers, status tags, and hints.
Do match shadow weight to height: shadow-sm for resting interactive, shadow-md for hover lift, shadow-lg for overlays.
Do keep body text at or below 65-75ch per line on content-reading surfaces.
Do use the emerald tint highlight (rgba(16,185,129,0.18), 4px radius) to mark the target word in example sentences.
donts: Don't add streaks, mascots, confetti, or gamified reward loops. Learning is the reward. (Anti-reference: Duolingo.)
Don't add gradient hero stat panels, word-count banners, or identical icon-grid card layouts. (Anti-reference: generic SaaS.)
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards or callouts.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text). Single solid color only; emphasis through weight or size.
Don't use success, danger, or warning colors as decorative accents. State only.
Don't add box-shadow to resting, non-interactive elements.
Don't animate layout properties (height, width, padding). Animate transform and opacity only.
Don't use modals as the first solution for inline actions.
